A UAE floating rate is 3-month EIBOR plus your bank's margin: EIBOR was about 4.45% at the 22 October fixing, as reported by a UAE mortgage broker, so a 1.50% margin gives 5.95%. Check the Central Bank of the UAE's published fixings and use the figures in your own offer.

    How Fixed-Rate Mortgages Work in the UAE

    Most UAE "fixed" mortgages are only fixed for the first part of the loan, commonly one to five years. After that, the loan reverts to a variable rate: EIBOR plus a margin. EIBOR moves with the market, while the margin is set by your bank and normally stays the same for the rest of the loan.

    So you are really choosing two prices at once: the introductory rate you see in the advert, and the reversion margin in the small print. On a 25-year loan with a 3-year fix, the reversion margin applies for 22 of the 25 years.

    In October 2026, UAE banks' published fixed rates ran from about 3.89% to 4.74% for fixes of one to three years, and their reversion margins from about 1.09% to 1.99%. With EIBOR near 4.45%, that puts reversion rates at about 5.5% to 6.4%, well above the fixed rates.

    How to Use This Calculator

    1. Enter the loan amount and term. If you already have a mortgage, use the outstanding balance and the years left.
    2. Enter the fixed rate and how many years it is fixed for.
    3. Enter the floating rate: 3-month EIBOR plus the margin in your offer. The fixed mortgage moves to this rate when its fixed years end.
    4. Compare the two columns: the monthly payment, total interest and total amount. Then try a higher and a lower floating rate.

    How the Comparison Is Calculated

    \1

    B is the balance when the rate changes, i is the annual rate / 12 / 100, and n is the months left. The fixed mortgage's payment is recalculated once, when its fixed years end, so both loans end on the same date.

    The floating rate is held at the level you enter for the whole loan. In reality it resets with EIBOR, usually every three months.

    Example: AED 1,500,000 over 25 years, fixed at 4.25% for 3 years, then floating at 5.95%. The payment starts at AED 8,126 and rises to AED 9,468 in year 4, an increase of 16.5%. Floating at 5.95% from day one costs AED 9,619 a month. Fixing first saves AED 93,397 in interest over the term.

    Should You Switch from Fixed to Variable?

    Paying to leave a fixed rate early rarely makes sense just because EIBOR has dipped, because the fixed period may be nearly over anyway. It can make sense when your fixed rate is well above current pricing and a new loan comes with a lower margin for the many years that follow.

    Count the cost of switching before you decide. The early settlement fee is capped at 1% of the balance or AED 10,000, whichever is lower, and a switch can also involve valuation, processing and mortgage registration costs. Ask for a full list and compare it with the saving the calculator shows.

    What This Calculator Leaves Out

    • Timing of payments: totals are simple sums, so a dirham paid today counts the same as one paid in 20 years
    • Refinancing later: many borrowers move to a new deal when a fix ends, which this does not assume
    • Rate changes: the floating rate is held at one level, but EIBOR moves, so try a high and a low rate rather than relying on one number
    • Fees: early settlement, processing and registration costs are not included
    • Islamic home finance: profit rates often follow the same pattern, but contract terms differ, so check how yours resets

    Frequently Asked Questions

    What happens when my fixed-rate mortgage ends in the UAE?
    The loan usually moves to a variable rate of EIBOR plus the margin set out in your offer letter. If 3-month EIBOR is 4.45% and your margin is 1.50%, you pay 5.95%. Your payment is then recalculated on the remaining balance and term, and it changes again as EIBOR resets.
    Is a fixed or variable mortgage better in the UAE?
    It depends on the rates you are quoted and where EIBOR goes. When introductory fixed rates sit below EIBOR plus margin, as many did in October 2026, fixing is often cheaper even if EIBOR falls. Enter your own offers above, then try a lower floating rate to see how far rates would have to fall for floating to win.
    How much is the early settlement fee on a UAE mortgage?
    The Central Bank of the UAE capped the fee on home loans at 1% of the outstanding balance or AED 10,000, whichever is lower, in a 2019 circular. Some lenders may set different terms during a fixed period, so check your own contract and ask for a settlement figure in writing.
    Can I switch from fixed to variable before my fixed period ends?
    Usually, by refinancing or by asking your bank to rebook the loan, though you may pay an early settlement fee and other charges. Enter your outstanding balance, the term left and the years left on your fix, then compare the saving with those costs to see if the switch pays for itself.
    What is the margin on a UAE mortgage?
    It is the bank's fixed percentage added to EIBOR. Published reversion margins ran from about 1.09% to 1.99% in October 2026. The margin typically lasts for the rest of the loan, so a small difference can matter more than a low introductory rate.
    What is a floor rate on a variable mortgage?
    It is the lowest rate the loan can charge, however far EIBOR falls. A loan with a 4.75% floor stays at 4.75% even if EIBOR plus margin comes to 4%. Not every loan has one. If EIBOR plus your margin comes to less than the floor, enter the floor as the floating rate in the calculator.
